chain.label: Line of thunderstorms and heavy rain showers crossing DFW runway 17L at the time of landing
chain.trigger: It was raining at DFW at the time of the landing, and there were numerous thunderstorms in the area.

chain.label: Right crosswind of 25-30 knots with a wind surge at the leading edge of the storm line
chain.trigger: AAL102 was subjected to a direct right crosswind of 25 to 30 knots

caused_by.evidence: Based on witness statements, radar data, and weather information, a wind surge was associated with the line of showers and thunderstorms moving across the airport.

chain.label: Wet, rain-swept runway 17L surface with marginal microtexture
chain.trigger: the tire marks noted on the runway were not caused by hydroplaning, but were instead erasure marks on the wet runway

caused_by.evidence: a line of moderate to heavy rain showers and thunderstorms was crossing runway 17L as AAL102 was landing

chain.label: American Airlines carried critical landing-roll directional control items only as 'techniques', not procedures
chain.trigger: American Airlines did not have procedures for: 1) Holding forward pressure on the yoke after touchdown; 2) Not using the handwheel steering control at high speeds; ... 4) Coming out of reverse into forward thrust to regain directional control.

chain.label: No training or standardization on DC-10 landing-roll control technique or on first officer backup duties after a captain takeover
chain.trigger: the Safety Board could find no reference to these procedures in American Airlines DC-10 Operating Procedures or training program

caused_by.evidence: The implication of citing an action as a technique, rather than as a procedure, could permit nonstandard use of critical flight control inputs by pilots during critical phases of flight, such as evident during this accident.

chain.label: Cabin emergency light battery packs improperly reassembled during airline maintenance
chain.trigger: the tap wire or primary lead was incorrectly soldered onto all four battery packs. In addition, individual battery cells were out of the original factory-assembled sequence.

chain.label: No approach, landing or go-around briefing conducted despite forecast thunderstorms at destination
chain.trigger: The accident crew did not perform an approach briefing.

caused_by.evidence: Safety Board investigators were unable to find specific American Airlines operations policy on when and where a captain should brief specific procedures, emergency or otherwise.

chain.label: Captain countermanded the first officer's go-around at about 50 feet agl and took control near 40 feet
chain.trigger: the first officer stated, 'I'm gonna go around.' The captain stated, 'No, no, no, I got it.'

caused_by.evidence: He did not want to make a missed approach and have to deal with the thunderstorm activity again.

After the captain countermanded his decision to go around on short final and took control of the airplane from him, there was no specific guidance to the first officer regarding his duties to back up the captain during the landing.

chain.label: Airplane landed long, 4,303 feet beyond the threshold and outside the 3,000-foot touchdown zone
chain.trigger: the airplane touched down, on the runway centerline, about 4,303 feet from the approach end of 17L

caused_by.evidence: By overruling the first officer's decision to abort the landing, the captain committed the airplane to landing long on a rain and crosswind swept runway.

chain.label: Captain failed to use proper directional control technique: released the yoke for handwheel steering, left rudder/elevator/ailerons near neutral and held full reverse
chain.trigger: He released the control column and used the nosewheel steering handwheel control ... the FDR indicates that there was little input into the flight controls to maintain the airplane on the runway.

caused_by.evidence: the airplane 'weather vaned' about 5 degrees to the right. He acted 'instinctively' to return to the centerline of the runway.
the Douglas precaution on the use of nosewheel steering was not included in the American Airlines 'Operating Procedures' for the DC-10
it left him with virtually no time to communicate with the first officer or flight engineer, or to assess conditions affecting the airplane

chain.label: Airplane yawed and tracked about 8-9 degrees right of runway centerline during the rollout without recovery
chain.trigger: the rudder and elevator positions approached neutral, and the airplane heading and ground track changed to the right

caused_by.evidence: the probable cause of the accident was the failure of the captain to use proper directional control techniques to maintain the airplane on the runway
the airplane's nose turned to the right, most likely due to the right crosswind acting upon the vertical stabilizer
the main landing gear tires had enough friction to allow cornering ... it tracked into the direction the nose was pointing
committed the airplane to landing long on a rain and crosswind swept runway

chain.label: Left main landing gear separated and nose gear folded aft in the soft soil, severing No. 1 pylon fuel and hydraulic lines
chain.trigger: The left main landing gear was found separated from the wing structure at the forward 'zero margin' trunnion pin and at the aft trunnion pin lug.

caused_by.evidence: After crossing the taxiway, the airplane returned to the soft soil and left deep trenches from all landing gears.

chain.label: Postcrash fire erupted aft of the left wing at the No. 1 engine pylon
chain.trigger: a large fire developed aft of the left wing of the accident airplane about the time it came to rest

caused_by.evidence: In the No. 1 engine pylon area, fuel and hydraulic lines, electrical cables, wire bundles, and fire extinguisher lines were severed at a point near the wing-to-pylon interface.

chain.label: Cabin emergency lighting failed to illuminate, leaving a dark cabin for the evacuation
chain.trigger: the power and charge level was not sufficient to illuminate the overhead and door emergency lighting system

caused_by.evidence: With the improper configuration, enough electrical power would have been provided to indicate an 'up system' in battery tests but not enough power to energize the emergency lights in the actual emergency.

chain.label: Airplane departed the right side of runway 17L at 95 knots, crossed taxiway 3S and came to rest in soft soil with substantial damage
chain.trigger: The right main landing gear departed the runway shoulder with the airplane's speed slowing to about 95 KIAS about 14 seconds after airplane touchdown.

caused_by.evidence: This track continued until the right main landing gear departed the right shoulder of the runway.

chain.label: Two passengers seriously injured and 38 persons minorly injured, mostly during the emergency evacuation
chain.trigger: Two passengers received serious injuries, and 35 passengers, 1 flightcrew member, and 2 cabincrew members received minor injuries during the evacuation of the airplane.

caused_by.evidence: most of the minor injuries and all of the serious injuries were reported to have occurred during the emergency evacuation

because the nose gear and left main landing gear were fractured, the airplane came to rest in an approximately 10-degree left wing down and slight nose-down pitch attitude ... the emergency evacuation slides, for the two right rear cabin exits, were deployed at nearly a vertical angle
the fire affected the urgency of passenger egress because it could be seen glowing through the left windows of a darkened aft cabin
The result was a darkened cabin after the airplane came to rest.
